Hello, Agents!

This roundup brings together the default-branch updates released on October 10, 13, and 16. These updates focus on quality of life, co-op interactions, save stability, and combat fixes. Thank you for continuing to share your feedback!
Before updating: Please finish your current run first, as updating may cause issues with in-progress runs.
Reduced the hold time for dismantling weapons and items from 2 seconds to 1 second, and shortened item pickup banner display times.
Added a tutorial skip option: when one save has completed the tutorial, players can choose to skip it for other saves that are still in the tutorial stage.
Added a confirmation prompt before abandoning the current run and returning to the bar from the main menu.
The safehouse now provides an exit to end the run when all boss portals are locked. The in-run timer also pauses in the safehouse, preventing boss portals from timing out while players wait.
Reduced Scream Soda's trigger cooldown from 3 seconds to 1 second.

Reduced the number of different agents required to clear the game for the related achievement from 10 to 3. Fixed incomplete progress tracking and added missing progress from existing historical clears.
Restored supported 16:10 display resolutions and improved the save selection layout on narrower screens.
Removed unnecessary network speed checks and the associated wait when entering the bar. Improved the bar HUD layout, and hid the countdown and red warning while Dark Zeus is locked.
Fixed Origin Shield's barrier not being restored correctly when continuing a run on a regular floor.
Fixed R-7 reviving with no shields when it had no health containers, leaving it unable to attack or take damage.

Fixed a brief attack-button press during Ascend's preparation phase failing to trigger a sword swing. Improved its attack direction and the orientation of its small flying swords when a target is locked.
Fixed abnormal lightning arcs involving Chidori Kunai's split projectiles, along with related projectile cleanup issues.
Fixed lightning strikes from Skyrend and standard projectiles from Jedon failing to trigger Popcorn correctly. Reduced instances of Origin projectiles damaging the player when combined with Popcorn.
Fixed melee attack intervals increasing at high attack speeds, and holding the fire button allowing shooting during reloads.
Fixed Glitz's projectile-count affixes and their upgrades not taking effect correctly, and corrected their co-op synchronization.
Fixed badge generation with Glass Dice. New badges now use the affix pool for the player's current weapon, falling back to the general pool if no eligible options are available.
Fixed item dismantling being interrupted, the same item being dismantled repeatedly, and dismantling an item disrupting subsequent pickups under certain conditions.

Improved enemy targeting and automatic attack target handling, reducing interference from certain enemy projectiles and unnecessary objects. Fixed targeting configurations for void eggs, certain egg-type enemies, and the second phase of the God of Screens fight.
Improved void enemy spawn effects and warnings for their death effects to make them easier to distinguish.
Reduced processing overhead in scenes with large numbers of projectiles.

Fixed basketballs becoming unresponsive after being taken by another player, remaining occupied after the player holding them disconnected, and the host being unable to pick up basketballs thrown by other players.
Fixed physics stopping on some liftable objects after they were left idle.
Improved simultaneous item pickup handling. Fixed inconsistent reward ownership when two players grabbed the same item simultaneously in a claw machine room.
Fixed gambling machines getting stuck when multiple players interacted with them simultaneously, and interaction issues when multiple players used a faith machine at the same time.
Failed attempts to use a dice machine no longer consume coins, keys, or free unlock uses.

Fixed inconsistent key and crystal consumption and door states when multiple players tried to unlock a door simultaneously. Fixed mismatched door states between the host and other players that could prevent passage.
Fixed gambling doors damaged by electricity no longer being destructible with explosions.
Fixed duplicate purchases of the same shop item and inconsistent restock states.
Fixed the floor number not matching the host's after reconnecting in Classic Mode, and incomplete restoration of some items, skills, and player stats when reconnecting.
Fixed the host being assigned the wrong P1/P2 identity in the bar, and room boundary protection being disabled too early when players occupied different rooms.
Fixed question marks spawned by butterflies in the Temple of Psychedelism failing to deal damage correctly, and some enemies unexpectedly regaining health after taking damage.
All players now use the host's difficulty settings for each minigame round. Fixed Hexjar minigame rooms remaining on the map after players left them.

Fixed corrupted local saves on Steam trapping players in a retry loop and preventing them from entering the game. If recovery is unavailable, players can choose to delete the affected local save slot and start over.
Fixed a potential crash when loading a save or continuing a run, save recovery failures under certain error conditions, and save notifications remaining visible after a save failed or was cancelled.
Fixed boss objectives not being restored correctly in some older saves.
Corrected the reward quantity for the Dance Party task.
Fixed dialogue display errors preventing the tutorial from progressing.
Fixed certain boss fights failing to progress to later phases under specific conditions, and issues when entering certain boss rooms. Improved stability during floor transitions.
Fixed old encounters still triggering completion after returning to the bar on death or restarting a run.
Fixed the portal used to end a run incorrectly taking players to the next floor after returning from a weapon upgrade room. Improved the placement of its interaction prompt.
Fixed teleport arrival points overlapping with the gathering area for returning in certain Temples of Faith and teleport rooms.
Fixed weapons not being locked correctly in basketball rooms generated by Hexjars, and a dance room machine interaction error disrupting subsequent pickups.
Fixed certain chests becoming impossible to interact with after quickly leaving a room in single-player mode.

Fixed the emote wheel's clickable area, character and emote previews remaining visible after switching screens, and recovery issues after certain navigation failures.

Improved handling of repeated clicks, confirmation, and back navigation on character, mode, difficulty, and level selection screens. Added the missing localized confirmation button to the Storm Breach level selection screen and updated some localized text.
Fixed players getting stuck on terrain, incorrect doors, and background and masking issues in certain rooms, including some trap rooms. Corrected some hairstyle configurations.

releases.displayName: A quick update about the in-game Chat function

items.text: Hey Agents. Today we’ve made the decision to remove the “free chat” feature within Neon Abyss 2. This isn’t a step we’re taking lightly, so we wanted to let you know a little more about the reasons why.

A big part of our work is making sure Neon Abyss 2 is correctly age rated, and that it complies with local laws wherever we launch. It’s one of those behind-the-scenes bits that we don’t often talk about.

A big part of this is the chat feature and how we successfully moderate it. Removing it isn’t something we’re loving having to do, but as a small team here at Veewo, it’s just not possible for us to keep that included and appropriately moderated especially as:
It would significantly affect the overall age rating
With the updating UK social media laws covering chat communication in video games, we would also need to include age-gating functions and age verification systems
It’s sadly not possible for us to effectively moderate a free chat function as well as ensure we comply with the understandable local laws - safety of our players is always a top priority.
To help, we’re instead focusing on the pre-set communications like emotes, to effectively allow you to communicate in multiplayer lobbies. We think this will help in a few ways:
Making communication much faster than manually typing
Meaning that players who speak different languages can still communicate effectively
As we create these, we can make sure they comply with age rating requirements
We hope you understand, and thank you for your support as we work to get Neon Abyss 2 ready for full release!

items.text: Yo Agents, it's time to get back in the Abyss! We've been busy adding a whole lot more to the Abyss as we storm on through our Early Access programme! We know, it's a Sunday - weird time for an update, right?
We've got four main parts to the default branch coming at you today:
The New Black Dog Bar
A Brand New Agent: Tino
A New Manager Boss: Dark Aphrodite
A New Regular Boss: God of Graffiti

The whole team at Veewo has been working ultra hard to raise the bar… and we don’t just mean on quality. Welcome to the all-new Black Dog Bar. To evade the clutches of Titan Group’s investigation, the team have relocated the Black Dog Bar to a remote desert area, hiding the Agent-filled action well beneath the undulating dunes.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45341641/1d7e959be0865b2716f28074879137250c3b594d.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45341641/5aa4ce90aa10cf0d621d6325dbe726e4af3ef979.png"]

Throughout Early Access we have given you more agents than you could shake a catgun at. R-7, Cassie and Mira have all joined the party, and now they’re super psyched to introduce you to Tino. A street-dwelling rapper whose pockets are always brimming with wonder, Tino uses melody and flow to blast a trail through the neon-drenched chaos.
His power lets Tino duplicate Wonder Jars (at the cost of a little life), and we hope you folks are going to show him a warm welcome down there!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45341641/bac2d550a79f1b2e94b57a58df79f97c6ec93ff7.png"]
Aphrodite already entered the Abyss in previous updates, but with a leaden edge, this new boss offers a new fight. Are you scared of the dark? Maybe you should be?

Aphrodite turns love on its head, weaving fantasies and desires to bewitch players and lead you to your doom. Can you break from her spell long enough to gain the upper hand? The journey to victory is lit by the neon lights of the Abyss, with the soft glow caressing Dark Aphrodite’s alluring silhouette. Each one of your hastening heartbeats is an offering at her altar - maybe it’s best to just stop beating altogether?
Unlock: Defeat regular Aphrodite.
Challenge: Defeat Hermes to enter next floor while having at least 10 Hatchmons.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45341641/4166c38b45ac32f4b006b4ab5fc6f1fa4d12c233.png"]

You better hope and spray you have a chance of defeating him. Prepare for a brush up (ok that’s the last of the painting puns) with destiny with the God of Graffiti. Use a special strategy or just spray and pray (ok that’s actually the last one)
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45341641/4b7ccfc7f6eb844605d043b4f71faa557b622488.png"]

To get prepped for part of the next MAJOR update, we’ve opened testing for the new Storm Raid game mode on the Beta branch as well - we also added a new switch function to the main menu to help players get over to the Beta Branch much easier..
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45341641/3b04f4f7a95d5b92cc55484404af7db1debc0cf4.png"]

Storm Raid is a faster, more streamlined mode with no dungeon exploration. Instead, you’ll focus on blasting your way through, entering battles, gaining upgrades, and pushing through stage after stage as the challenge ramps up.
Try it out and let us know your feedback, issues, and suggestions so we can keep improving the mode.

We've already begun work on the full version - it's a huge amount of content as well as development and optimisation across different platforms (say no more - wink wink). As such this stage of development is going to be in flux, and we don't want to make promised dates for you and then miss them.

We'll be releasing updates regularly around internal milestones from now until the 1.0 version launches, and we'll keep you in the loop as to what's happening over on social media and in Discord, too.

We'll have more news about 1.0, which platforms we're releasing on, and a more accurate release window in the near (ish) future, so stay tuned! For more updates fans can follow the official X account, and join the official Veewo Discord.
The Whole Team at Veewo Games!

releases.displayName: We May (Will) Delay - Update Pushed to June

items.text: Hey Agents! We’re sorry to mess you around a little, but we have a little pushback news for you today. It turns out that adding a whole new game mode as well as a new Agent is a LOT of work (who knew?!) and we’re postponing the May update a little - which should land with you in June.
We know it’s not the news you wanted, and to be honest it’s not the news we wanted to give. BUT, we also don’t want to ship you folks subpar updates either, so here we are.

The next major update will be landing in June, and to say thank you for your patience we’ll be including an additional TWO bosses alongside the rest of it. We do also have more surprises planned for you in the summer, but we’re not ready to share those just yet (otherwise they wouldn’t be surprises, obvs).

Anyway. We hope you’re not too mad, and that the extra content in June will make up for it a little, at least. In the meantime, you CAN still get involved with new content as some of the new elements of the “May Update” will be making their way into our Beta branch right now!
The Beta is open for anybody who owns Neon Abyss 2, and to get there you just have to
Right click Neon Abyss 2 in your Steam library
Go to Properties
Hit up Game Versions and Betas
Select the Beta!

The game will need to update after you do that, but we hope that our loyal Agents will drop in. The Beta branch is a little more unstable, but it means that you can give feedback on upcoming features, and further help to shape Neon Abyss 2!

So another huge thank you to all who have taken the time to jump into the Abyss and leave some feedback already! We’ll be back with more news soon and in the meantime, we’ll catch you on the flip side, nerds!

releases.displayName: Fire Support - Major Update is Live

items.text: Hey Agents!! We’ve got a Big One for you today with the Neon Abyss 2 Fire Support update, our first major patch since Early Access release. We’ve got a couple of brand new elements added here, as well as a huge number of fixes and balances for a bunch of weapons.
The Fire Support patch is live NOW, after testing in our Beta Branch over the weekend. The highlights include:
The New Blackdog Patch System – allowing players to pick a starter build to jump in with, following failure in the Abyss
Weapon Fixes and Balancing – we’ve been listening to your feedback and have a huge list of weapon tweaks and fixes
Visual optimisation and improvements – for multiple visual effects and artwork
New Items! – adding a little more spice to the Abyss

If you played back at launch, there’s a whole lot more to jump in with now, as well as ongoing fixes and improvements (it’s Early Access, right?!). Let us know how you find the new Fire Support patch and we’ll continue to throw tweaks, fixes, improvements and balancing at you in the coming weeks before our NEXT Major Update.

This all-new system lends a hand to players after a losing run in the Abyss (and we know there are a few of you out there! Sadly, me included). This new ability can be unlocked within the first page of the Evolution Tree, allowing a little leg up for those that fancy it. After losing a run, players will be thrown a random weapon / item bundle, specially bolted together by our Abyss Architects.

Agents who complete an Abyss run with their random item bundle from the Blackdog Patch will unlock it to be able to select in future – meaning that you can choose to select that again (after failure in the Abyss), or get another random Patch to try out a new combination and try and unlock that one, too.

notes.title: Comprehensive Weapon Adjustment, Optimisation and Balancing

items.text: We’ve been listening to your feedback, and one of the things you’ve really let us know about is that weapon balancing has been feeling a little off in the Abyss. We’ve been taking some time to add a butt-load of new tweaks (and fixes) for a huge number of weapons.

All of these changes are in addition to our new Damage system. While we’re not giving you the ins and outs on exactly how this works (we need to keep SOME things aloof and mysterious) we’re hoping that this will help with weapon balancing, and all weapons have had stats tweaked to essentially improve the fun factor – though we’ll let you be the judges of that.

We’ve put a (partial!) list of these within the more patch-notes style bit just below, but do also keep in mind that the team are constantly working on weapon tweaks and balancing within regular updates. Your feedback is not only welcome, but critical to these balancing patches, as we need to know what you like and don’t like. We can’t promise to make every tweak (as one Agent’s Abyss Trash is another Agent’s Abyss Tresure) but we’re using feedback heavily to plan and prioritise balancing.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45341641/cd45f6bf2d83a319a9bebc6f36e2cabdfdcd31da.png"]

The Abyss is meant to be chaotic, that’s the point of the Abyss, and it only gets crazier with multiplayer co-op. But we’ve heard your feedback, and we do agree that it needs to be manageable chaos at the very least (for reference, see the weird scene with Jeff Goldblum in the original Jurassic Park movie where he’s dropping water on Laura Dern’s hand).

So we’ve been making changes to how the chaos gets represented in game. We’ve toned down player effect animations, and increased visibility of enemy projectiles as well. All of this aims to keep the chaotic feeling of the Abyss, while making sure you can see what you’re doing and what’s going on around you.
We’ve also added new high-definition pixel art for all weapons , just to help the Abyss get a little extra shine.
After searching the forums, it looks like you all really wanted new items which helped you to get more jump boxes, so we’ve added 94 new items to help you get additional jumps!

I really need to point out that this is a joke, just for anybody who thinks we’re being serious. We’ve not added jump boxes, but we HAVE added a bunch of new items which improve attack speed, range and trajectory aiming, which we hope to help you feel a bit more buffed up in the Abyss.
Seriously, though. If you do want more jump boxes, just say. We’ve got so many going spare and we can just throw them into the Abyss any time.
The (Blackdog) Patch notes

So. That’s the narrative. But if you’re the type of Nerd that likes a bullet point list, we’ve got your back. Here it is in all it’s stunning glory. The Patch Notes for our first major patch, the Fire Support Update.
New Blackdog Patch Mechanics

VOLTEDGE - Mechanic Change: Charge time no longer decreases continuously, but each slash's damage increases progressively.

Hey Agents! We're back once again for another daily patch. As we plaster the walls of the Abyss with changes, we wanted to send another thank you for the tireless efforts that you've been putting in yourselves. You've left some incredible feedback so far, and the team here are working to get as much of it into the Abyss as possible.

We can't get to everything straight away, but the team has been working to make sure we're answering the constructive feedback in-game, and not just here with words. We're got a light touch on the Default branch today, but we've also moved a good number of bug fixes over into the Beta branch for testing. A fair amount of this focus has been directed towards the (multiple, sorry) issues related to the "Continue Game" feature, and networking connectivity.
We hope you'll continue to live, laugh, level your way through the Abyss. Here's what's been deployed in today's patch.
Fixed an issue where the Continue Game feature would reset badge levels to 1.
Fixed issues related to picking up blank badges and badge upgrades.

Fixed an issue with the "Continue Game" feature where the level of Foundry Badges was incorrect and set effects would grant rewards repeatedly. (you probably liked that, but we're still taking it away)
Fixed an issue where James' inventory was incorrect after continuing a game.
Fixed an issue where weapon badge levels were not correctly synced when continuing a game.
Fixed an issue where force-quitting the game with a full Faith bar could cause an abnormal Faith status after continuing the game.
Fixed a bug where gambling machines would still incorrectly deduct money.
Fixed an issue where purchasing items from the shop would fail when carrying the "Festival Red Packet" relic.
Fixed an issue where the QTE UI would freeze if the input device (keyboard/controller) was switched while the QTE prompt was on screen.
Fixed an error in the shield acquisition order of the Dawn System.

Fixed an issue where rapidly clicking the "Continue" button on the results screen could cause the character to disappear after returning to the bar. (wouldn't be the first time I'd ghosted my friends at the bar)
Fixed an issue in multiplayer mode where the loading screen would get stuck if a teammate disconnected while entering the next level.
Fixed an issue where the flying ability would be lost after quickly entering and leaving a shop room.
Fixed other potential issues that could cause game errors, improving overall stability.

Added a network region system. Players will now connect to corresponding servers based on their geographical location (Asia, Europe, Americas) for a more stable online experience. Cross-region matchmaking will not be available.

So that's all we're deploying today, but we hope you continue to have a great time in the Abyss. "Oh, but how do I join the Beta Branch", you ask? well I'm GLAD you asked because I've already typed it and it would be a shame to waste it.

Well, Agents. It’s nearly a week since we went live with Neon Abyss 2 and we have yet another update which hopes to tweak, balance, change and apply a fresh coat of glow in the dark paint on the walls of the Abyss.
We’re just updating the Default Branch today, and should have some more content for our plucky (and totally Rad) Beta Testers coming soon™.

We don’t have a Beta Branch update today as we’re working out some Glitches in the Matrux (shush you. We don’t want a lawsuit). But you can still play in the Beta Branch if that’s your thing. Just select it as your option by heading over to:
Library – Right click Neon Abyss 2 – Properties – Betas

And selecting the Beta Branch from the drop-down menu. There’s no password, but bear in mind that the Beta Branch is for more frequent and less tested updates, and will likely be less stable than the default branch.

Hey Agents. Another day and another update for the Abyss.

We’ve been making progress against a lot of the things you’ve been reporting so far, and the first thing we wanted to do today was send a continued thank you for taking the time to come and leave feedback – both constructive and positive. It’s really important for Neon Abyss 2’s continued evolution, and we can’t thank you enough.

There are a few of your pressing issues which we’ve taken steps to fix in 7.21 which have gone live in the default branch. We also wanted to give a reminder that if you’d like to test faster fixes (but maybe a little more disruptive environment) we also have the Beta Branch available!
So, let’s get to it. What’s been changed in the Abyss in 7.21?
The Error Recovery button now also fixes weapon jamming (being unable to fire)

While we conduct internal testing, our limited experience in developing online multiplayer games has led us to adopt a cautious approach to avoid introducing new issues via rushed fixes. To address this, we’ve launched a Beta branch. This branch will receive daily updates to rapidly resolve reported issues and optimize gameplay, though it may be less stable. If you prefer faster update cycles, you can switch to this branch.
For the default branch, we will only deploy urgent bug fixes immediately, while non-critical fixes will follow a weekly update schedule to ensure a more stable experience.
